title: Router: canActivateChild can't find guard provided in own module
body:
<!--


**Current behavior**

<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->

When trying to use a children guard (canActivateChild) in the same module where the guard is provided, the guard fails to be injected.

`Error: No provider for ChildGuard!`

If we provide the guard in a parent module, it works.
If we provide the a canActivate guard in the same module where it is used, it works.

**Expected behavior**

<!-- Describe what the behavior would be without the bug. -->

The guard should be injected and work like the canActivate guard.

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**

<!--
If the current behavior is a bug or you can illustrate your feature request better with an example, 
please provide the *STEPS TO REPRODUCE* and if possible a *MINIMAL DEMO* of the problem via
https://plnkr.co or similar (you can use this template as a starting point: http://plnkr.co/edit/tpl:AvJOMERrnz94ekVua0u5).
-->

Demo can be found here: ~~http://plnkr.co/edit/JeLBnEgkoaHh4wDe9MAd?p=preview~~ http://plnkr.co/edit/vc35AC1UIbZtlp0IjekX?p=preview
1. Click on "Go to route with child guard" button.
2. See error in console: Error: No provider for ChildGuard!

What happens:
- when click on the button, router navigates to /admin
- AdminModule provides ChildGuard service
- Default route in AdminModule (empty) uses ChildGuard `canActivateChild: [ChildGuard]`

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**

<!-- Describe the motivation or the concrete use case -->

I have to protect all the child routes using a guard that is only known by that module, loaded by lazy-mode.

**Please tell us about your environment:**

<!-- Operating system, IDE, package manager, HTTP server, ... -->

Windows 10 Enterprise
Chrome 53.0.2785.116 m (64-bit)
IIS
- **Angular version:** 2.1.0
- **Angular version (router):** 3.1.0
